title: Digital Disease Monitoring in Patients with Cardiovascular Diseases
summary:
Cardiovascular diseases demonstrate a high and steadily increasing prevalence in the general population and are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Consequently, early identification of clinical deterioration, continuous assessment of the disease course, and evaluation of treatment response are of paramount importance.
Conventional cardiology diagnostics often provide only momentary snapshots of a patient's health status during isolated clinical encounters. In contrast, consumer-grade smartwatches facilitate the non-invasive, continuous assessment of cardiac and functional parameters in real-world settings over prolonged periods. These metrics include heart rhythm, heart rate, heart rate variability, physical activity, and sleep patterns. However, the clinical utility of continuous smartwatch-based monitoring across diverse cardiovascular cohorts remains insufficiently investigated.

interventions.name:
This is a prospective, multicenter, non-interventional observational study designed as a feasibility and validation study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients capable of providing informed consent
•	Age > 18 years
•	Written informed consent
•	Diagnosis of a cardiac condition based on prior routine diagnostics—e.g., patients with cardiovascular disease (including coronary artery disease), patients with primary non-ischemic cardiomyopathies (e.g., DCM, HCM), or patients with known atrial fibrillation (e.g., prior to planned, clinically indicated ablation therapy)
•	Paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation (not permanent), i.e., generally suitable for rhythm control
•	Willingness and ability to wear the smartwatch (Withings ScanWatch2) continuously during daily activities throughout the study period
Exclusion criteria:
•	No personal smartphone on which the necessary app can be installed
•	Lack of informed consent
•	Unwillingness or inability to use the smartphone app
•	Any comorbidity that impairs understanding or successful participation in the study. The decision is made at the discretion of the investigators.
